## Work Experience

**Bioinformatics Research Assistant (**Aug. 2023 – Present)

*Department of Bioinformatics and Computational Biology, University of North Carolina, Charlotte, North Carolina*

-   Leading a project with the goal of building a pipeline for structural variant genotyping using pangenome graphs, integrating tools like vg toolkit, Minimap2, Cactus, etc.

-   Employed statistical and machine learning methods such as Wald’s test, hypergeometric test, regression, and principal component analysis (PCA) to uncover novel biomarkers and mechanisms underlying complex biological processes.

-   Led a project that constructed a pan-transcriptome and used it in a bulk-RNA seq data analysis pipeline, processing multi-terabyte datasets and uncovering 70% more differentially expressed genes compared to when the conventional pipeline that involves a single reference genome was used.

-   Utilized several R and Python packages for data processing and visualization, generating publication-ready plots.

-   Presented findings to diverse audiences – including academic collaborators, industry stakeholders, and interdisciplinary teams – through meetings, technical reports (peer-reviewed publications), non-technical reports, and professional conference presentations.

-   Expedited computationally intensive tasks by leveraging HPC environments, reducing runtimes by up to 80% through parallel processing.

-   Developed a workflow and documentation for the easy utilization of a legacy bioinformatic tool, reducing setup and execution time by 50%.
